questions.question: Convert infix A+B*C to postfix.
questions.solutionApproach: * has higher precedence than +. B*C first: BC*. Then A+: A BC* +.

questions.question: Evaluate postfix expression: 6 3 2 * -
questions.solutionApproach: Push 6, push 3, push 2. See *: pop 2,3 → 3*2=6, push 6. Stack: 6,6. See -: pop 6,6 → 6-6=0 (second-popped minus first-popped: 6-6). Wait — pop order: last pushed popped first. Stack after * is [6(orig),6(result)]. Pop top=6(result), pop next=6(orig): compute second_popped - first_popped = 6-6=0.

questions.question: Input pushed in order 1,2,3,4. Is the output sequence 3,4,2,1 achievable via stack push/pop?
questions.answer: Yes, achievable: push 1,2,3; pop→3; push 4; pop→4; pop→2; pop→1.

questions.question: How would you design a stack that supports PUSH, POP, and GETMIN, all in O(1) time?
questions.solutionApproach: Maintain a second auxiliary stack that tracks the minimum seen so far at each level. On PUSH(x): push x onto main stack; push min(x, auxTop) onto aux stack. On POP: pop both stacks together. GETMIN: just peek aux stack's top.
questions.answer: Use a parallel auxiliary 'min-tracking' stack, pushed/popped in sync with the main stack — GETMIN = peek aux stack top, O(1).
